_doc: Gate config for examples/scripts/audit_gate.py. Copy to your vault root as
gates.json (or pass --config) and describe YOUR checkers. This is a template, not a
drop-in: the commands below point at this repo's example tools.
name   used inside finding keys. Keep it stable - renaming a gate makes every one of
its findings look brand new, and the gate will block on all of them at once.
cmd    argv list. {python} is the running interpreter, {vault} the vault root. A
relative path resolves against the folder holding THIS config file.
parse  how output becomes finding keys:
json:<field>         stdout is JSON; take the list at <field>
json:checks[].list   flatten the named lists out of a list of check objects
lines:<regex>        each matching stdout/stderr line (group 1 if present)
Keys must be stable between runs. Anything volatile - a timestamp, a duration,
a run id - makes an old finding look new forever, and a gate that cries wolf
every turn is a gate somebody switches off.
paths  glob patterns; the gate runs only when a matching file changed. Use it to keep
a slow suite off the critical path. Omit it (or use **) to always run.
cwd    optional working directory; defaults to the folder holding this config.
